The user wants me to transcribe both pages of this OIML Certificate of Conformity into GitHub-flavored markdown, with tables as HTML, including all text including embedded text in images (like the eagle logo — I should note it, but there's no text in it... Actually the eagle is the German federal eagle "Bundesadler" logo — it contains no text, but I should mention it as an image description? The rules say text embedded in images must be transcribed. The eagle logo has no text. But I could include an image reference or alt text. Best practice: include the image as markdown image with alt text, e.g., ![Bundesadler (German federal eagle logo)](...). Similarly the circled "III" accuracy class markings — those are text "III" in a circle, which I should transcribe as III, perhaps with notation like ⊙III or (III). I'll use ㏒... no. I'll write it as "III" within a circle representation — maybe use the unicode ⊙ or just write (III). Common transcription: "③"? No. I'll use "⊙ III" or just "III" in parentheses: (III). Let me use "Ⅲ" in a circle: ⃝. I'll write it as "(III)" — but to be faithful, maybe I can use the character Ⓜ style... There's no circled III unicode. I'll transcribe as "III" with a note-free representation: use "(III)". Actually the instruction says not to annotate. So just transcribe the text "III". The circle is a graphic. I'll render as "III" — perhaps 〷 no. I'll just do "III" inside parentheses to indicate the circle: (III). Hmm, but that could be seen as annotation. It's fine.
